- SDR: you can now transmit with a HackRF, only where it is allowed: your call sign and an amateur radio licence are needed on the amateur bands (set in each tool's settings), and every transmission is checked against the bands first. Talk from the microphone in Listen (NFM, AM, USB, LSB), send your position beacon from APRS, send a photo from SSTV (Robot 36, Martin M1, Scottie S1, PD120), and let the radio join the Meshtastic mesh as a node (it announces itself and sends the phone's position). Receiving stays the default and nothing goes out unless you ask
- SDR: a new automatic gain, over the radio's whole range, tested against a simulated front end. It climbs little by little when the signal is weak, comes down at once on a strong one, and no longer stops at LNA 24 / VGA 20. One profile per tool (narrow signals, wide channels, ADS-B pulses, broadcast FM)
- SDR: the tools are sorted in category cards (General, Aviation, Sea & rescue, Mesh & LoRa, Satellites & weather, Home & sensors, Voice & pagers); Wi-Fi and Bluetooth tools get category tabs
- ACARS: the decoder now reads the bits the way aircraft send them, so real messages come through
- Listen: zoom from 2 MHz to 125 kHz, tuning steps from 100 Hz, many more stations in tabs (shortwave broadcast, amateur bands, air and sea…), "Auto" step that follows the broadcast spacing, the passband shadow in USB and LSB
- Spectrum: zoom, a marker with its frequency and level, and a "Listen here" button; the header shows the range of the radio plugged in
- SDR settings: a converter offset for an up- or down-converter (Ham It Up, SpyVerter or any value)
- Bluetooth: a new smart glasses detector (Ray-Ban Meta, Oakley Meta, Snap Spectacles, HeyCyan, Vuzix…), with the evidence for each match, a confidence, an alert distance and a background watch. It says camera-capable glasses are in range, not that they are recording
